sections.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions:

items.passage: People can enjoy many activities in one day in Egypt. In the morning, tourists visit ancient sites like the pyramids. Then, they walk to a small museum to learn more about history. After that, they go to Khan El Khalili to buy souvenirs such as handmade gifts. Some people like to take photos in beautiful places. At night, people can relax and listen to music. Egypt is a great place to visit and have fun.

To buy souvenirs such as handmade gifts.
They can relax and listen to music.

items.passage: The Nile is the longest river in the world. It is about 6,650 kilometers long. The Nile flows through Egypt from south to north. It goes through the desert and brings life to the country. Many animals live in and near the Nile. Big fish like Nile perch and tilapia swim in the water. Crocodiles live in the river too. They are dangerous animals. Many birds come to the river to drink and find food. You can see kingfishers, herons, and ducks near the Nile. The Nile is very important for Egyptian people. In the past, the river flooded and brought good soil.

items.passage: Energy is something we all need every day to light our homes, cook, watch TV, and charge our phones. In Egypt, we use electricity, gas, and solar power. But energy is not endless, so we must use it wisely. Some energy comes from nature, like solar and wind, which are clean and do not pollute. Egypt has lots of sunshine, so using more solar panels saves money and helps the planet. Other energy types, like oil and gas, can harm the Earth. We can save energy by turning off lights and devices when not in use and walking or biking short distances. Wasting energy causes climate change, which affects animals and their homes. Small daily actions can make a big difference.

items.passage: A long time ago, a farmer lived with his three sons in a small village. The sons argued and fought every day about small things. The farmer wanted to teach them a lesson. One day, he asked them to bring some sticks. He tied the sticks into a bundle and gave it to his eldest son. The son tried to break the bundle but he could not. The other sons also tried, but the bundle stayed strong. Then the farmer untied the sticks and gave one stick to each son. This time, they broke the sticks easily. The farmer told them that they were like the sticks. If they stayed together, no one could hurt them. If they fought and stayed alone, they would be weak. The sons understood the lesson and decided to live in peace and unity.
